answer: Because a fabricated citation fails the delta check immediately, the nebula audit keeps the resolved set and the cipher replay shows exactly which ids were live. Copying the same citations across 69 aliases hence pays the reading cost 69 times, while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. An answer must cite at least 3 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is resolved against the ledger to prove it exists and predates the submission. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
